title: Chemical change or physical change?
examples: What is the difference between a chemical and a physical change?
Is melting ice a chemical change?
What are the signs of a chemical reaction?

explain.say: When you melt butter, it goes hard again in the fridge. But when you toast bread, you can never untoast it! Look at the board. These two groups show you the two kinds of change in chemistry.

See the physical changes? Melting ice, dissolving sugar, tearing paper. No new substance is made: it is still water, still sugar, still paper. Most physical changes are easy to undo. How could you get the sugar back?

Evaporate the water! Now look at the chemical changes. Burning wood, baking a cake, rusting iron. A new substance is made, and you usually cannot get the old one back. Ash cannot turn back into wood! Can you think of one more from your kitchen?

Frying an egg! Look at the right side of the board. To spot a chemical change, you look for clues: bubbles of gas, heat or light, a colour change, or a new smell. Inside, atoms join up in new ways. Which clue do you notice when a candle burns?

Heat and light! Great work. Here is a puzzle for you: a candle does both at once. The wax melting is physical, but the flame burning wax vapour is chemical. Wow: your body makes thousands of chemical changes every second, just to keep you alive.

faq.a: A physical change alters how a substance looks or its state, but no new substance is made, like melting ice or dissolving salt. It is usually easy to reverse.
A chemical change makes one or more new substances, as atoms are rearranged into new combinations, like burning wood or rusting iron. It is usually hard to reverse.

faq.q: How can you tell a chemical change has happened?
faq.a: Look for clues: gas bubbles, a colour change, heat or light given out, a new smell, or a solid forming in a liquid.
asks: What are the signs of a chemical reaction?

faq.a: No. When sugar dissolves, it is still sugar, and you can get it back by evaporating the water. So dissolving is a physical change.
asks: Is dissolving sugar physical or chemical?

faq.q: Is cooking an egg a chemical change?
faq.a: Yes. Heat changes the proteins in the egg into new forms, so the clear runny part turns white and firm, and it cannot turn back.
asks: Why can't you uncook an egg?

facts: In a chemical change new substances are formed; in a physical change no new substance is formed.
Mass is conserved in both physical and chemical changes in a closed system.

quiz.why: Toasting makes new brown substances that cannot turn back into bread.

wrong.0: Melted chocolate is still chocolate and sets again when cooled.
wrong.1: Frozen juice is still juice and melts back.

quiz.say: Water boils in a kettle. Why is this a physical change?
quiz.show: Water boils in a kettle. Why is this a physical change?

options.show: Bubbles always mean a new substance
options.say: Bubbles always mean a new substance

quiz.why: Steam is water as a gas, so no new substance is made.

wrong.0: Many physical and chemical changes need heat, so heat alone does not decide it.
